answer: Men are biologically hardwired to lead and protect, which is why most positions of authority are still dominated by them; the core skills required for leadership simply occur more reliably in males. Women, on the other hand, have inherited historically more indirect roles, such as caregiving and artistry, and different genes mean they usually avoid activities that involve planning or probability. Since men no longer need large families to guarantee reproductive success, they can still protect women so traditional male roles should continue.
